title: Derived site comparison preserves evaluation into the coefficient unit
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring and Y a scheme. In the ordinary derived categories of small etale and pro-etale A-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], let C be exact comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], t its canonical derived tensor comparison, and c:C(A_Y) ≅ A_Y its canonical coefficient-unit comparison. For any Q,K and e:Q → A_Y, one has t_{Q,K};((C(e);c) tensor 1);lambda_{C(K)} = C((e tensor 1);lambda_K). Tensor is the ordinary K-flat derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. No exceptional inverse image, compact support or projection formula occurs.

source.place: lemma-pullback-tensor-product (Stacks Tag 07A4), its proof on K-flat complexes; unit coherence for its degreewise tensor map. Also sites-modules.tex, lemma-tensor-product-pullback.

proof.text: Choose K-flat models for Q and K. Comparison is exact and preserves flat objects, and therefore carries these models and their direct-sum total tensor to the defining comparison models. The characterizing square of leftDerivedTensorComparison identifies the tensor comparison on these models with the degreewise ordinary sheaf tensor comparison.

Naturality in Q moves the arrow e through this tensor comparison. At Q equal to the coefficient unit, the canonical coefficient-unit comparison followed by the left unitor is the image of the etale left unitor: both send each pure tensor a tensor k to a k, including the total-complex differential signs. The unit is concentrated in degree zero.

The resulting equality on K-flat representatives descends along localization and the characterizing square to the stated equality in the derived category. Zero objects and the zero coefficient ring obey the same formulas.
